summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, and a history of kidney and pancreas transplants was admitted for blood transfusion and dialysis after missing her appointment. She developed transfusion-associated circulatory overload with acute respiratory distress and was found to have urosepsis from E. coli, requiring ICU care and Meropenem. Preoperative evaluation revealed severe mitral regurgitation and coronary artery disease, leading to MV repair, CABG x5, and closure of a patent foramen ovale. Postoperatively, she experienced complications including right leg cellulitis, Klebsiella UTI, respiratory failure requiring re-intubation, and pleural effusions managed with pigtail drains. She gradually improved with dialysis, antibiotics, and rehabilitation, and was discharged to extended care with stable cardiac function, healing incisions, and a plan for ongoing monitoring and physical therapy.
